query: Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state and a target density below 6 g/cm3, what single intervention could overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation while improving room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts measurable changes relative to the as-processed baseline, defines the relevant composition, temperature, exposure-time, and test-environment boundaries, cites supporting evidence from previously reported Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys, and proposes a controlled experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a targeted alloying element can stabilize a non-equilibrium solid solution, enhancing the performance of Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state
generation.intervention: Addition of a specific alloying element (e.g., Zn, Ca, or Sr) to stabilize the solid solution
generation.conditions: Target density below 6 g/cm3, room temperature, and exposure to air or a controlled environment
generation.structural_mediator: Stabilization of the non-equilibrium solid solution
generation.mechanism: Suppression of stable intermetallic formation, leading to improved compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation
generation.predicted_outcome: Enhanced room-temperature compressive behavior, improved corrosion resistance, and increased resistance to high-temperature oxidation compared to the as-processed baseline
generation.boundary: Composition (Mg content, alloying element addition), temperature (room temperature to high-temperature oxidation), exposure time, and test environment (air or controlled environment)
generation.uncertainty: Lack of specific data on the effects of targeted alloying elements on the performance of Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with varying alloying element additions and testing of room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of the targeted alloying element does not result in significant improvements in compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance, the hypothesis is falsified.
